markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize a controlled change to BERT4Rec’s training objective: **constant-mixture reconstruction and recency-balanced terminal supervision**.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Strong reconstruction margins coexist with recommendations described as broadly relevant but unnecessary. Training discrimination therefore does not establish current usefulness. (2) Users identify stale interests and fulfilled needs as recurring problems. Recent-prefix supervision could emphasize changing intent, although purchase necessity remains unobserved. (3) Industrial_and_Scientific has 10.15% small-margin positions and user RankMe 21.53 versus item RankMe 48.38. These justify monitoring difficult terminal predictions, without diagnosing collapse.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already includes last-item masking. Terminal supervision is an established ingredient, so the contribution here is a controlled sampling and loss-balancing experiment. (2) [Masked History Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23649) motivates shifting emphasis toward next-item learning. Its decoder setting does not establish that a curriculum benefits this encoder. (3) [TiSASRec](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/wsdm20b.pdf) models interaction intervals. This motivates a later temporal-attention experiment within BERT4Rec, using historical timestamps only.

**Framework and candidate ideas.** Separate three intervention axes: supervision alignment, supervision scheduling, and temporal representation. Evaluate one axis at a time before combinations.

Scores are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Constant mixed loss with recency-balanced cutoffs | 3/7/7/7/3 | Small change; addresses stale influence and weak current relevance; directly trains terminal discrimination | Established masking ingredient; recency can miss durable interests; gains unproven |
| Increase terminal weight over epochs | 4/7/7/7/4 | Tests whether progressive alignment improves current relevance and terminal separation | Adds scheduling choices and confounds; can forget reconstruction benefits |
| Learned historical time-gap attention bias | 4/8/8/5/6 | Can distinguish episodic activity from persistent interests | Larger architecture and predictor change; temporal proximity does not establish usefulness |

**Selected experiment.** Keep the corrected backbone and inference unchanged. Sample terminal cutoffs from an equal mixture of uniform eligible positions and the last min(10, number of eligible positions). For cutoff t, expose only history before t, append MASK, and supervise item t. Separately compute ordinary masked reconstruction. Optimize L = 0.5 mean(L_reconstruction) + 0.5 mean(L_terminal).

This targets two user failures: stale historical influence and broadly related recommendations lacking a current reason for selection. It also targets weak positive–negative separation, particularly in Industrial_and_Scientific. These are hypotheses; exact compatibility and fulfilled demand remain unresolved.

Use seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Retain all four categories, fixed splits, preprocessing seed 0, and one checkpoint per category. Select using pinned macro validation HR@10; report terminal margins separately from reconstruction probes. No improvement is claimed before measurement.

idea.description: Train the supplied BERT4Rec with an equally weighted, separately normalized mixture of ordinary masked reconstruction and terminal-mask prediction on strictly truncated training prefixes. Draw terminal cutoffs from a fixed 50:50 mixture of uniform eligible cutoffs and the most recent ten eligible cutoffs.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale historical influence and broadly related items without a compelling current purpose. Prefix-only terminal supervision could improve sensitivity to recent intent while reconstruction retains access to enduring interests. Industrial_and_Scientific's 10.15% small-margin rate motivates measuring whether terminal discrimination improves; existing reconstruction margins cannot establish next-item ranking quality.
idea.implementation_notes: Implement as a sampler/loss change against the host-supplied corrected baseline; no baseline source was provided here. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], existing routing and artifact paths, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Use one jointly trained BERT4Rec and one selected checkpoint per category. Split each existing batch between reconstruction and terminal examples to keep the number of encoded sequences fixed. Normalize the two objectives separately using the baseline's existing loss. Terminal cutoffs require at least one preceding interaction; remove the target and every later interaction before encoding. Reserve room for the appended mask by retaining at most L-1 preceding items. Left-pad and read the maximum nonpadding index. Keep the baseline reconstruction corruption policy. Since the architecture and inference are unchanged, retain the matching predictor writer and checkpoint format. Preserve ModelView and DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, plus diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Keep the loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L; terminal positives occupy only the appended-mask position. Report terminal probes with an explicitly constructed terminal loader rather than inferring corruption branches from unmatched bookkeeping. Never use validation interactions for training, unseen future timestamps, unavailable metadata, separate scoring components, or another trial's checkpoints.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category, initialize the corrected BERT4Rec with seed 42.
For each epoch <= 200 and each of 200 batches:
  Allocate half the existing batch to baseline masked reconstruction.
  For each remaining example:
    Sample a training user with at least two interactions.
    Let E be target indices having at least one preceding interaction.
    With probability 0.5 sample t uniformly from E;
    otherwise sample t uniformly from the final min(10, |E|) indices.
    x = left_pad(history[max(0, t-(L-1)):t] + [MASK], L).
    positive = zeros(L); positive[final_nonpadding_index(x)] = history[t].
    Sample negatives using the unchanged valid baseline rule.
  Compute reconstruction and terminal losses separately.
  loss = 0.5 * mean(reconstruction_loss) + 0.5 * mean(terminal_loss).
  Update the single model.
Use the host's fixed validation protocol to select checkpoints.
At inference, append MASK to the observed history and score from its final nonpadding state.

originality.positive: The fixed recency-balanced cutoff distribution and explicit loss normalization form a clear, falsifiable adaptation to the supplied baseline.
originality.negative: BERT4Rec already uses last-item masking; mixed reconstruction and next-item supervision is established.

future_potential.positive: Provides an interpretable control for later curriculum and temporal-attention experiments under the same single-model constraint.
future_potential.negative: Recent positions can overrepresent short-lived activity, and improved terminal training margins may not improve validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires localized sampler and loss changes while retaining the backbone, inference path, and checkpoint structure.
code_difficulty.negative: Prefix truncation, left padding, loss normalization, and diagnostic separation need careful implementation to prevent leakage or misleading measurements.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Uses appended-mask next-item inference and supplementary last-item masking.
limitations: Random reconstruction can use right context unavailable during next-item inference.
Its findings do not establish the proposed cutoff mixture's benefit under the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: From Past To Path / Masked History Learning
contributions: Provides precedent for combining historical reconstruction with next-item learning and progressively emphasizing the latter.
limitations: The supplied search summary describes a generative decoder setting; transfer to BERT4Rec remains a hypothesis.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models pairwise historical interaction intervals within attention.
Motivates a later temporal representation intervention.
limitations: Its causal backbone must not replace BERT4Rec in this task.
Historical intervals cannot establish compatibility, ownership, or current purchase necessity.
